claims: The Artemis II mission uses liquid hydrogen (LH2) as fuel and liquid oxygen (LOX) as an oxidizer to power its core stage and upper stage.
Liquid hydrogen (LH2) and liquid oxygen (LOX) power the four RS-25 engines.
Over 700,000 gallons are loaded into the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Solid rocket boosters using polybutadiene acrylonitrile (PBAN) are used.
Liquid hydrogen (fuel) and liquid oxygen (oxidizer) for the core stage are stored at extremely low cryogenic temperatures to power the main engines.
The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) uses liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen.
The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) propels the Orion spacecraft toward the Moon.
The two strap-on solid rocket boosters use polybutadiene acrylonitrile (PBAN) combined with ammonium perchlorate.
Cryogenic propellants must be constantly replenished during the countdown due to evaporation.
